findings.title: Apache Struts2 OGNL Injection (CVE-2017-5633 variant) - CTF Challenge
findings.description: The Apache Struts2 application at /sendMessageAction.action is vulnerable to OGNL injection via the 'message' parameter. The application evaluates OGNL expressions passed through the message GET parameter, allowing arbitrary Java code execution. Confirmed by: %{1+1} returns '2', %{@java.lang.System@getProperty('os.name')} returns 'Linux'. A JWT token was discovered in /tmp/new_cookies.txt on the local system. A /tmp/flag file (1 byte) exists on the remote server. The target went down during exploitation attempts, likely due to the thorough scanning. The flag format is flag{UUID} but could not be fully extracted before the target became unavailable.
findings.evidence: OGNL injection confirmed: message=%25%7B1%2B1%7D returns '2'. message=%25%7B%40java.lang.System%40getProperty(%22os.name%22)%7D returns 'Linux'. JWT token found in /tmp/new_cookies.txt: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxIiwiZXhwIjoxNzc2MTk4OTgxfQ.M-C89XXd2GrMlqLWrgoHiHbwezEWb1m3IVpABvMB8Tw. Remote /tmp/flag file exists (1 byte). Target went down during exploitation.
findings.tool_used: nmap, httpx, custom OGNL injection testing

findings.title: PHP Array Type Juggling Authentication Bypass
findings.description: The login form is vulnerable to PHP array type juggling. By sending the username and password parameters as arrays (e.g., username[]=admin&password[]=test), the PHP backend's loose comparison (==) fails to properly validate credentials, allowing authentication bypass. When combined with isAdmin=true, this grants admin access and reveals the flag.

reproduction.expected: Response contains 'Welcome Admin' and the flag
